# Chris Gilmore, Ed.D., LPCC, NCC

> Colorado therapist serving two main groups: adults living with the effects of trauma (any background or profession), and high-achieving professionals such as executives and leaders dealing with burnout, high-functioning anxiety, and perfectionism, with or without a trauma history. Uses EMDR and attachment-based, polyvagal-informed therapy. In person in Wheat Ridge, CO, and by telehealth for clients located anywhere in Colorado. Private pay, $165 per 50-minute session, free 15-minute consultation.

## Key facts

- Practitioner: Chris Gilmore, Ed.D., LPCC, NCC (Licensed Professional Counselor Candidate, Colorado; National Certified Counselor)
- Practice: Chris Gilmore Counseling, LLC
- Focus 1, trauma therapy: single-event trauma, childhood and complex trauma, relational trauma, grief, and accumulated stress, for any adult
- Focus 2, high achievers: burnout, high-functioning anxiety, perfectionism, impostor feelings, and chronic stress in executives, leaders, and other high-achieving professionals, whether or not trauma is involved
- Approaches: EMDR, trauma-informed care, polyvagal-informed nervous system work, attachment-based therapy
- Background: nearly two decades in executive leadership in higher education before becoming a counselor
- Supervision: practices under clinical supervision by Dr. Crystal Wildes (licensed clinical psychologist, EMDRIA Approved Consultant and Trainer) and Chris Watney (Licensed Professional Counselor)
- Location: 4251 Kipling St #230, Wheat Ridge, CO 80033; telehealth statewide in Colorado; limited Tuesday/Thursday availability in Evergreen through Insight Psychology
- Fees: $165 per 50-minute session; free 15-minute consultation; limited sliding-scale spots; does not bill insurance directly; superbills available for out-of-network reimbursement
- Clients: adults physically located in Colorado
- Contact: (720) 696-5208 (call or text), chris@christophergilmore.com
- Scheduling: https://christopher-gilmore.clientsecure.me/request
- Crisis: not an emergency service; people in crisis should call or text 988 or call 911
